poem: Your hand finds mine in the quiet dark, and the whole world softens into one warm room. Here, beside you, I have finally come home.
Morning slips through the curtains like a held breath, and there you are, sleepy and golden. I want every sunrise to find us just like this.
You taught me that love need not be loud. It can be two mugs of tea, a shared blanket, and a rainy afternoon with nowhere to be.
I have loved you in the hush of winter and the bloom of spring, and I will love you in every season the years still hold.
Your laughter is my favorite room in the house, the place where every worry hangs up its coat and stays a while.
We are two lanterns side by side, and the dark has never looked so small.
When you rest your head against my shoulder, I understand what the stars have been whispering all along.
Some men search the world for treasure. I only had to turn my head and find you, steady and bright, beside me.
Let the evening settle slowly over us, your fingers in my hair, my heart keeping time with yours.
Love, for us, is the small things: your coat on my chair, your song half-hummed in the kitchen, your name the first thought of my day.
You are the lamp left on in the window, the promise that wherever I wander, someone gentle is waiting.
Between your heartbeat and mine there is a language no one taught us, and we have spoken it fluently since the very first hello.
I would trade a thousand grand adventures for one slow Sunday with you, the radio low and the window open to the rain.
Your eyes are the color of safe harbors. I drop anchor there every night and sleep without fear.
Hold me the way the sea holds the shore, again and again, patient and certain, never once letting go.
We built a small world out of ordinary days, and somehow it grew large enough to hold all of my joy.
Your kindness is a quiet fire. I have warmed my hands at it through every cold year, and it has never dimmed.
If love is a garden, then you are the sunlight and the patient rain, and I am the happiest thing that ever bloomed.
In a crowded room my eyes still look for you first, the way a compass leans toward home.
The kettle sings, the candle glows, and your feet are tucked against mine beneath the blanket. This is what heaven feels like.
I fell in love with the way you listen, as though every word I speak were a small and precious thing.
Come close, my love, and let the night be soft. There is nothing left to prove, only your warmth and my gratitude.
You are the paragraph I reread when the world turns noisy, the line that tells me I am loved.
Together we walk the long road home, two shadows leaning into one, and every step is lighter for having you.
Your name tastes like honey on my tongue, and I say it softly just to feel the sweetness settle.
Hand in hand beneath the autumn trees, we gather golden leaves and golden hours, and call it all our own.
I never knew a heart could feel like a fireplace until I learned the glow of yours.
Every scar I carry softened when you touched it, and now they read like roads that led me here, to you.
Tonight the moon leans in the window just to watch us, two quiet men who found the whole sky in each other.
You make the ordinary shimmer: a grocery list, a late-night drive, a shared umbrella in the rain.
Let others chase the thunder. I have found the gentler miracle of your breathing beside me in the dark.
My love for you is not a flame that flares and fades but an ember, banked and glowing, warm through the longest nights.
You are the first page of every story I want to live, and I mean to read them all with you.
In the quiet after laughter, when your head finds my chest, I hear the world say yes.
I am softer because of you, braver because of you, and more myself than I have ever been.
Snow falls on the sleeping town, and inside, your arms are the only winter I will ever need.
We dance in the kitchen to a song only we can hear, and the floor turns into a small and perfect galaxy.
You are my favorite hello and my hardest goodbye, and the sweetest in-between of every day.
I keep your voice like a pressed flower, folded in the pages of my memory, fragrant whenever I need it.
Rest here, beloved. The day has asked enough of you. Let my arms be the shelter and my heart the hearth.
Two toothbrushes in a single cup, two names on one small door. What a quiet, wondrous thing it is to belong.
The sea may be vast and the sky may be wide, but nothing compares to the width of my love for you.
When you smile, the room remembers how to be warm, and so do I.
I would follow the sound of your humming through any dark, certain it leads to the place where I am home.
You are the soft landing at the end of every long day, the exhale I did not know I was holding.
Our love is a slow river, unhurried and deep, carrying us gently toward whatever tomorrow brings.
The stars have had ten thousand years to practice shining, yet none of them are as bright as the look you give me across a quiet room.
I plant my gratitude in the soil of your hands, and every day it grows into something green and tender.
Wrapped in wool and lamplight, we read in silence, your ankle hooked over mine, and this is all the poetry I need.
Love found us not with trumpets but with a quiet knock, and we opened the door and never looked back.
Your heartbeat is the metronome of my best days, steady and sweet, setting the tempo of my peace.
I am rich in a way no ledger can measure: I have your morning voice, your evening hand, your whole unguarded heart.
Let the world turn however it pleases. In the circle of your arms, time stands politely still.
You walked into my life like spring walks into a field, quietly, and suddenly everything was blooming.
Every ordinary evening becomes a feast when you are across the table, laughing at your own joke before you finish it.
I love you in the language of small kindnesses: the tea left warm, the porch light on, the blanket drawn over my shoulders.
Under the quilt of night we trade our secrets softly, and the dark becomes the gentlest confessional.
You are the quiet in my noise, the north in my wandering, the yes at the end of all my questions.
Wherever your hand rests, the world grows kinder. I have mapped my whole life to the warmth of your palm.
We grow old the way ivy climbs a wall, slowly, gracefully, holding on to each other all the way up.
Your forehead against mine, our breath mingling in the cold, and for one sweet moment the universe is only us.
I wish I could bottle this evening, the lamplight, the music, your head on my shoulder, and open it on every hard day to come.
Love is the way you remember how I take my coffee, and the way I remember the song that makes you cry.
You are my favorite season, the one that arrives gently and lingers long, golden at the edges, warm to the core.
On the porch at dusk, fireflies rise like small blessings, and you lean into me as though the night were made for this.
I did not know that home could be a person until I found your laugh, your arms, your steady and welcoming heart.
When the world grows sharp, I think of you, and every edge turns to velvet.
Our hands fit together like two halves of a sentence that took a lifetime to finish.
You give me the kind of love that does not ask me to shrink, only to rest, to breathe, to be wholly and gladly known.
The rain taps its fingers on the glass, and we, wrapped close, whisper that we have never been more content.
I will be the shoulder for your weary days and the laughter for your bright ones, now and for all the days between.
Your love is a soft lamp in a long hallway, and I have never once been afraid of the dark since.
Come, sit beside me on the edge of evening, and let us watch the sky change colors, as quietly in love as the first day we met.
I treasure the way you hum while you cook, off key and utterly certain, filling the house with your sweet, ordinary joy.
Some loves are fireworks, brief and loud. Ours is a lighthouse, steady through every storm, forever guiding me home.
You turned my solitary years into a story with a happy ending, and then you kept writing, one tender chapter at a time.
In your arms the clocks forget their work, and an afternoon can last a gentle lifetime.
I love the crinkle at the corner of your eyes, the proof of every smile you have ever shared with me.
We exchange no grand speeches, only a look across the room that says, I am here, I am yours, and all is well.
Love, to me, is a quiet street at midnight and your hand tucked into my coat pocket against the cold.
You are the sweetest accident of my life, the wrong turn that led me to exactly where I belonged.
Under a sky full of borrowed light, we make our own, one soft word, one gentle touch, one lasting promise at a time.
The whole world seems to exhale when you walk in, as though it too had been waiting for your warmth.
If I could give you anything, it would be the way you look to me at the end of a long day: glowing, grateful, and wholly mine.
I keep a quiet place inside my chest that smells of rain and cedar and you, and I go there whenever I need to feel safe.
Our love is not a thing we found but a thing we built, brick by gentle brick, until it became the house we both call home.
Even in silence, your presence is a song, soft and sure, and I find myself swaying to it all day long.
You are the dawn I did not know I was waiting for, and now I wake each day already smiling.
Tucked beneath the same worn quilt, we trade the warmth of our feet and the secrets of our hearts, and nothing else is needed.
I will love you through the gray days and the golden ones, through the quiet years and the laughing ones, until the last page is turned.
The garden is overgrown and the kettle is late, but you are here, and it is the loveliest afternoon of my life.
Your name is a lullaby I sing to myself, and the music of it carries me gently into sleep.
Maybe the stars are only lanterns hung by those who loved as we do, to light the way for all who follow.
Look how the candlelight makes a halo of your hair. I am a lucky man to be loved by something so near to gold.
We have no need for poetry, you and I, for we live it: in the shared glance, the folded laundry, the hand that reaches in the dark.
When I think of forever, it has your face, your laugh, and the soft weight of your hand in mine.
You are the gentle answer to every question my heart has ever asked, and I will spend my days saying thank you.
Let us grow old in a little house by the sea, with salt on the windows and your hand always within reach of mine.
Tonight, as the world grows quiet, I whisper into the dark what I whisper every night: thank you for loving me, and for letting me love you.
And when the last light fades and the long day is done, may I find myself where I have always belonged: in your arms, in your heart, at home.
